title: Avatar
lead:
An Avatar is a graphical representation of a user, team, or entity.

Avatar can display an image, icon, or initials, and supports various sizes and shapes.

examples.name: Name
examples.description: The name is used to determine the initials displayed by the Avatar. It is also read by screen readers.

examples.name: Image
examples.description:
An avatar can display an image.
It is recommended to also include a name in addition to the image: the initials from the name are displayed while the image is loading, and the name makes the Avatar accessible to screen readers.

examples.name: Icon
examples.description: An avatar can display an icon. The icon will only be shown when there is no image or initials available.

examples.name: Badge
examples.description: An avatar can have a badge to indicate presence status. See the PresenceBadge component for more info.

examples.name: Badge Icon
examples.description: An Avatar can have a custom icon inside the badge.

examples.name: Shape: square
examples.description: An avatar can have a square shape.

examples.name: Color: brand
examples.description: An avatar can use the brand color from the theme's palette.

examples.name: Color: colorful
examples.description: An avatar can have the color be automatically picked based on the `name` prop (or `idForColor` can be used if a name is not available).

examples.name: Color: named color
examples.description: An avatar can have a specific named color from the theme's color palette  (e.g. `seafoam`, `grape`, or `pumpkin`)

examples.name: Active
examples.description: An avatar can communicate whether a user is currently active (for example, speaking or typing). Avatar supports `active`, `inactive`, and `unset`. The default is `unset`.

examples.name: Active Appearance
examples.description: An avatar can have different appearances when `active="active"`. Avatar supports `ring`, `shadow`, and `ring-shadow`. The default is `ring`.

examples.name: Initials: Custom Initials
examples.description:
An avatar can display custom initials by setting the initials prop. It is generally recommended to use
        the `name` prop instead, as that will automatically determine the initials and display them.

examples.name: Size
examples.description:
An avatar supports a range of sizes from 16 to 128. The default is 32. 

Avoid using sizes 16 and 20 for interactive Avatars, or ensure that there is at least 8px or 4px spacing respectively to meet WCAG target size requirements.
